title: tsParticles MCP HTTP requests can exhaust memory or terminate the server
summary: The MCP HTTP handler buffers request bodies without a size limit and parses JSON without a request-local error boundary. Large bodies exhaust memory; malformed JSON can terminate the process.

severity.rationale: Unauthenticated HTTP callers can deny service to one MCP server. The demonstrated impact is availability, so the rubric assigns 30 days.

affected.note: Body buffering: below 4.3.1; malformed JSON: through 4.3.0.

exposure: HTTP mode is exposed to reachable callers. The official Docker image enables HTTP mode by default.

remediation.details: Upgrade @tsparticles/mcp-server to 4.3.1 or later and replace running instances.
remediation.risk: Medium. Updating or containment can interrupt dependent workflows.

verification: Confirm the installed and running component meets the documented fix or containment condition.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted for independent review.
